desc:
Wix app maintenance and updates keep an older app working as Wix changes around it. Ecom Swift LLC runs a fixed care sprint: updating packages and the SDK, fixing open bugs, testing install and uninstall, and writing a short health report.

## What is Wix app maintenance?

Wix app maintenance is the routine work that stops an app from drifting out of date. It covers dependency and SDK updates, bug fixes, dashboard component updates, checks in the current editor and tests of the install, update and uninstall flows. It does not add new features. It makes sure the features you already have keep working.

## Why apps decay without upkeep

Wix updates its SDK, its dashboard components and its editor on a regular basis. An app that was fine when it launched can slowly develop problems: a deprecated method that now warns, a dashboard component that looks out of place, a widget that behaves differently in the current editor, a package with a known security fix you have not applied.

None of these announce themselves. Owners notice a glitch, shrug, and remove the app. By the time a support email arrives, several problems may have piled up, and fixing them together costs more than fixing them in turn.

## How upkeep protects your app's results

A maintained app keeps its listing credible, its widgets stable and its billing working. Billing deserves special attention. If the plan or upgrade flow breaks after a platform change, you lose revenue without any visible error.

Maintenance also cuts the cost of future work. A codebase on current packages is easier to extend, easier to hand to a new developer and less likely to block an App Market update. We cannot promise that Wix will keep every feature, but regular checks mean you find out sooner and have time to react.

## What a good maintenance sprint includes

- A version check of the SDK and every package in the project.
- Updates to the packages that matter most, starting with security and compatibility.
- Fixes for open bugs your users have reported.
- Dashboard components moved to current versions where they have changed.
- A check of site widgets in the current editor.
- Tests of install, update and uninstall on a development site.
- A test of the billing and plan flow.
- Error logging, so future problems leave a trace.
- A check that data collections can be backed up.
- A short health report with what was done and what still needs attention.

## How we run the sprint

We start by reading the project and listing everything out of date, with a note on risk for each item. We update in small steps and test after each one, so any problem can be traced to its cause. Then we test the full lifecycle on a development site, from install through use to removal.

The Basic package handles the version check, the most urgent updates, a lifecycle test and a report. Standard adds more packages, a few bug fixes, dashboard component updates and a billing test. Premium adds a framework upgrade to the current CLI, more bug fixes, error logging, a backup check and an upkeep plan for the months that follow. This is a one-time sprint, and ongoing monthly care is quoted on its own.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Send a list of known bugs with how to reproduce them.
- Tell us which features earn the most revenue, so we test those first.
- Keep a backup of your repository before we begin.
- Plan to repeat a light check after major Wix announcements.

**Avoid:**
- Updating every package at once without testing.
- Ignoring warnings in the console because the app still runs.
- Waiting for a user complaint before checking billing.
- Treating one sprint as permanent. Platforms keep moving.

## Who this is for

An owner of an app that has not been touched for a long time. A team without a developer who needs it kept alive. A founder who got a warning about a deprecated feature and wants it handled.

## What we need from you

Repository and Dev Center collaborator access, given by invitation. We never need your password. Also send known bugs, your current plans and a way to reach you if we find something urgent.
